npcs.name: Captain Veleth Adren
npcs.greet: Rations are counted by the bowl, sera. The count is not for sale, and neither am I. State your business and keep to the left.

npcs.name: Foreman Gorm Stonehand
npcs.greet: The ebony does not care who digs it. The foreman does. Mind the ledger; mind your feet. Both are slippery.

npcs.name: Ashlander Tuvi
npcs.greet: I trade at the gate and sleep outside it. The walls are not built for me. They are built for what I carry in my tongue: news.

npcs.name: Tindra Hael
npcs.greet: Tindra's Salvage and Salt. Whatever the mine spits out, I price. Whatever the sea spits out, I price twice. Ask nothing; owe nothing.

npcs.name: Sister Ilvani
npcs.greet: A chapel of one hall. A congregation of forty, on a good Sundas. The ash makes them pious, and the cold makes them punctual.

npcs.name: Rolan the Dockhand
npcs.greet: The wharf is rough planks and rougher manners. If you fall in, shout. If you shout, it is already too late. Mind the bollards.

npcs.name: Elder Hjalmgerd Fire-Warden
npcs.greet: The fire has burned since before my grandmother's grandmother. It does not need me. I need it. Sit, if you will. The wind is going to take a while.

npcs.name: Aslfur Wide-Eye
npcs.greet: I brought a horn from the north shore. It is a good horn. Do not ask what animal. The animal has asked me not to say.

npcs.name: Wren Wind-Listener
npcs.greet: The wind has been quiet since Sundas. A quiet wind is an animal holding its breath. I should like to know what it is waiting for.

npcs.name: Bodil Hide-Scraper
npcs.greet: Pelts, bone needles, drying racks, boat-oil. We trade at the south gate, in the Skaal way: no haggling, but a great deal of silence.

npcs.name: Torvald Boat-Mender
npcs.greet: I patch the hulls the sea has opinions about. It has a great many opinions. I am the only one who answers it politely.

npcs.name: Little Ketil
npcs.greet: Wren says the wind has a name. I think it is Frodi. I told Wren. Wren did not say no.

npcs.name: Skald Hrolf Iron-Brow
npcs.greet: A hall is only as good as its last hunt. Mine was a boar. A boar! Sit. There is mead, and there is still a beast out there with my name on it.

npcs.name: Ingrid Bone-Singer
npcs.greet: Sit. I am about to sing the death of a bear who never existed, in a fight that did not happen, to a crowd who will weep. It is called the craft.

npcs.name: Odd the Brewer
npcs.greet: My mead is honest. My dice are not. Come, a game: a drake a throw. Do not look at my left hand. It has been the same hand for sixty years.

npcs.name: Brynja Trail-Reader
npcs.greet: Tracks in the snow are letters, sera, written in a language older than speech. Most people read them and see only mud.

npcs.name: Sigrun Rib-Wright
npcs.greet: I hang the ribs, I mend the beams, I sharpen the spears that did not kill the beast the first time. Mind the whalebone. It has opinions.

npcs.name: Magister Ildar Neloth-Kin
npcs.greet: My uncle is brilliant and insufferable. I am brilliant and merely petulant. Do not confuse the two; he does not like it, and neither do I.

npcs.name: Apprentice Duvren
npcs.greet: Fetch this, carry that, do not touch the mushroom with the ribbon on it. I have been here two years. I have touched the mushroom with the ribbon on it.

npcs.name: Yarda Net-Girl
npcs.greet: I fish. I listen. I sell what I hear to whoever pays in coin or in cake. The Magister pays in neither; he pays in being surprised.

npcs.name: Pelli Sporeheart
npcs.greet: Mind your step. The gills are moist and the moss has teeth. Did you wipe your boots? You did not wipe your boots.

npcs.name: Commander Lucan Hale
npcs.greet: The wall holds. The wall always holds. It is the only thing in Frostmoth that behaves. State your purpose and wipe your boots.

npcs.name: Signaller Tisa Verrin
npcs.greet: Blue lantern, two flashes, wait; three flashes, run. If you see five, the gate is open and I have not opened it. Mark the time.

npcs.name: Chef Orsk Pot-Boiler
npcs.greet: Boiled barley, boiled mutton, boiled something I will not name. It is the garrison's idea of variety. Sit. You look underfed.

npcs.name: Armourer Decimus Ravo
npcs.greet: Imperial steel, Imperial rivets, Imperial cold. Nothing I make ever feels like a luxury. It feels like a promise.

relics.name: The Missing Tally
relics.desc: A foreman's tally-stick notched forty-one times; the last seven notches are scraped away with a knife.

relics.name: The Waking Spike
relics.desc: A rod of black ebony as long as a forearm, humming faintly, still warm from the deep.

relics.name: Sentries' Orders
relics.desc: A sealed order: "Hold until relieved." The date is long past; the ink is fresh.

relics.name: The Missing Verse
relics.desc: A bone slip scratched with a verse older than the village; the last line is half-eaten by damp.

relics.name: The Teller's Drum
relics.desc: A hide drum no larger than a bowl, still tuned to a rhythm nobody remembers choosing.

relics.name: The Great Beast's Tusk
relics.desc: A tusk as long as an arm, yellowed and scored with marks that look suspiciously like a count.

relics.name: The First Rib-Beam
relics.desc: A great curved whalebone beam, scarred and stained, the first rib ever hung in the hall.

relics.name: Glow-Gill Cap
relics.desc: A palm-sized fungus, teal and orange, still pulsing in time with your heartbeat.

relics.name: Whisper-Moss Tuft
relics.desc: A grey tuft that seems to hush the air around it.

relics.name: Ember-Stalk Spore
relics.desc: A warm red spore-bulb that gives off the faint smell of toasted bread.

relics.name: The Gate Pin
relics.desc: A heavy iron pin, as long as a forearm, the retaining pin of the gate. The cold has scarred it with fresh tool-marks.

relics.name: Sledge of Supplies
relics.desc: A hide-lashed sledge: barley, salt, lamp-oil and a crate of dressing for a garrison on short rations.

quests.title: The Spoil Heap Question
quests.offer: You count well, I assume? Anything beyond your fingers?
quests.pitch: The foreman reports the mine at nine dead since Frostfall. I count fourteen graves. The difference is five men, and the foreman's hand shakes when I ask. Walk the diggers' barracks, count who's missing, and tell me what is under that heap before the Redoran Council arrives and asks me the same thing.
quests.desc: Captain Veleth of Raven Rock's bulwark counts more dead miners than Foreman Gorm reports. She wants the difference explained.

objectives.text: Ask Foreman Gorm to count with you
objectives.topic: Nine, you said. The Captain counts fourteen.
objectives.reply: Fourteen. Fine. Fourteen. Five of them did not die in the mine. They walked into the lower gallery after the second collapse, and did not come out, and I did not stop them. They said the digging was singing to them. Here is the tally. I scraped seven notches. I am sorry.

objectives.text: Find the collapsed lower gallery at the foot of the shaft
objectives.journal: The headframe creaked in the wind. Below it, the shaft descended past a landing hung with lanterns, then a landing without. Somebody had nailed a board across the third level: "Do not listen."

objectives.text: Clear the gallery of what the digging has woken
Take the humming spike from the cracked wall
Face what the spike was holding in
Report to Captain Veleth
objectives.topic: The spoil heap, Captain. Five men, a humming spike, and something that I have put down.
objectives.reply: Then the mine is cursed or merely haunted, and I do not have the staff to tell which. The Council will ask me whether to seal the shaft or to break the mine's curse. I would like to say: you tell me. You are the one who has stood in it.

choices.label: Seal the shaft. The ebony is not worth it.
choices.reply: Then Raven Rock loses its income, and keeps its people. I will write that I sealed it myself, to spare you the hate.

choices.label: Break the curse. Keep the mine open.
choices.reply: Then I shall keep the lanterns lit and the miners few. Pray it holds. I will not.

quests.outro: Raven Rock sleeps, and some say it listens.

quests.title: A Hollow Quiet
quests.desc: The shaft is sealed, but the five men are still unaccounted for, and families want the bodies.

objectives.text: Speak to Sister Ilvani about the families
objectives.topic: The shaft is sealed. What do the families want?
objectives.reply: They want the names carved, and the bodies buried beside them. We can do the first. For the second, someone must go into the lower gallery before the seal is placed. I would not ask a stranger. I am asking.

objectives.text: Recover the five miners before the seal is set

quests.outro: The names are carved above the bulwark gate, five in a row.

quests.title: The Ebony Vigil
quests.desc: The mine stays open, with a night-watch set to keep the humming quiet.

objectives.text: Set the night-watch with Foreman Gorm
objectives.topic: The mine stays open. I will keep the watch with you.
objectives.reply: You are a braver fool than I. Take the third landing at midnight. If it sings, hum back. I have no better advice.

objectives.text: Hold the third landing against what answers the hum

quests.outro: The watch holds. The mine is quieter than it has been in a year.

quests.title: A Dispute Over Planks
quests.offer: You look dry, which is rare. Do you have a mind for arbitration?
quests.pitch: Two crews, one wharf. The ash-yam farmers claim the south planks; the net-men claim the north. There is a tide-mark on every plank and neither side agrees which it is. I have been punched by both. Settle it, or give me a good excuse to be on the next boat.
quests.desc: Rolan the dockhand wants a wharf dispute between ash-yam farmers and net-men settled.

objectives.text: Ask Tindra Hael who actually owns the planks
objectives.topic: Who built the wharf?
objectives.reply: The Redoran Council, with a cargo of timber from a Skaal trader. The Council wrote a lease and lost it. The Skaal trader kept the copy. Find the Skaal at Tel Mithryn's ferry, if you must, or ask Ashlander Tuvi, who remembers everything for a bowl of soup.

objectives.text: Ask Ashlander Tuvi what he remembers
objectives.topic: The wharf lease. What did it say?
objectives.reply: North planks for the net-men, south for the yam-boats, and the middle plank, a single plank, for whoever arrives first at dawn. It was a joke the Skaal trader made. Both crews have been fighting over a joke.

objectives.text: Walk the wharf at dawn and mark the middle plank
objectives.journal: Both crews arrived at the same moment, glared, and sat down, one on each side of the plank. The plank, I noted, is somewhat comfortable.

quests.outro: The middle plank now has a bench on it, and both crews sit there at dawn arguing about something else.

quests.title: The Sentries on the Windward Wall
quests.offer: Can you stand watch in the cold? The dead do not stay still.
quests.pitch: The windward wall has two sentries too many at the second bell. They wear Redoran colours older than the bulwark, and they stand where no one built a post. The living guards will not relieve them. The dead will not leave. Someone must ask them what they are waiting for.
quests.desc: Sister Ilvani asks you to speak with two spectral sentries on the windward wall.

objectives.text: Keep watch on the windward wall at the second bell
objectives.journal: Two shapes stood at the parapet, helmets turned toward the sea. One of them lifted a hand, and pointed to a hollow in the wall.

objectives.text: Take the sealed orders from the hollow in the wall
Bring the orders to Sister Ilvani
objectives.topic: Two sentries, a hollow in the wall, and these.
objectives.reply: Orders to hold the line until relieved. They were never relieved. Their commander died before he could cancel them. Give me the paper; I shall read it aloud, at the second bell, with a lantern. Then they may go home.

quests.outro: The windward wall is, at last, only a wall.

quests.title: Telling at the Fire
quests.offer: You listen like someone raised by storytellers. Are you?
quests.pitch: The Telling is a hundred verses long, and ninety-nine are known. The hundredth went out of Chief Frodi's mouth with his last breath, and nobody caught it. At the next dark moon we must tell all hundred at the fire or the fire will forget us. Gather the tellers' stories, find what was lost, and bring it home.
quests.desc: Elder Hjalmgerd needs the lost hundredth verse of the Skaal Telling before the dark moon.

objectives.text: Hear Aslfur's tale of the horn
objectives.topic: Elder Hjalmgerd needs the story of where the Telling broke.
objectives.reply: I was there when old Frodi died. His last words were a name: Haknir. Not a man. A shoal. He said, 'Tell it at Haknir's Shoal where the horkers sing.' Take my horn. It is the right pitch.

objectives.text: Hear Torvald's tale of the shoal
objectives.topic: Aslfur says Frodi named Haknir's Shoal.
objectives.reply: The shoal is where my father lost a boat and found a song. A bone slip lies in the old cairn there, if the horkers have not eaten it. They are polite. They are not honest.

objectives.text: Hear Wren's tale of the wind
objectives.topic: The wind is quiet. Does it know the verse?
objectives.reply: It knew it. It is holding it. The wind will not release a word until it is asked in the right place, with the right voice, by someone who has listened to all three tellers. You have. Go.

objectives.text: Go to Haknir's Shoal where the horkers sing
objectives.journal: The horkers lined the shore like a congregation. One had a bone slip at its feet and watched me with shrewd, patient eyes.

objectives.text: Take the missing verse from the cairn
Return the verse to Elder Hjalmgerd
objectives.topic: The verse is whole. The last line is damp. Which shall we tell?
objectives.reply: It reads: 'And the old chief was glad, for he had never meant to win.' Written, it is noble. Told as it happened, Frodi lost the fight and was glad because he lost. The Telling has always been written. Shall we tell it as written, or as it happened? You are the one who found it. You choose.

choices.label: Sing it as it was written. The noble ending.
choices.reply: Then the Telling is whole, and kind to the dead. It is a good ending. It is not a true one. I will tell it in my sleep, and know.

choices.label: Sing it as it happened. The honest ending.
choices.reply: Then the Telling is whole and hard. Chief Frodi lost and was glad. The village will gasp. It will remember. It may even be better for it.

quests.outro: The hundredth verse was spoken at the fire, and the wind began to blow again.

quests.title: A Trophy That Is Wrong
quests.offer: You have the eyes for it. Look at this horn and tell me what is wrong.
quests.pitch: I took this horn from a horker bull on the north shore, a good bull, a fat bull, and the horn has runes on the inside. Dunmer letters. Not Skaal. Somebody carved a horker, years ago, and let it live. Somebody wanted it to be found. I would like to know who, and why.
quests.desc: Aslfur Wide-Eye took a horn from a horker and found Dunmer runes carved on the inside.

objectives.text: Ask Ashlander Tuvi to read the runes
objectives.topic: These runes. Can you read them?
objectives.reply: A Dunmer fisherman's mark and a debt: 'I owe the bull one favour.' He tamed a horker pup, carved the horn, and set it free. The bull has been waiting, I think, to repay it. Look for a hut on the eastern headland.

objectives.text: Find the fisherman's hut on the headland
objectives.journal: A sunken hut, a lone chair, and a mouldering Dunmer coat on a peg. On the table, a bowl of fish with a rune drawn beside it. The bull had been leaving a fish each morning.

objectives.text: Tell Aslfur what the horn meant
objectives.topic: The horn was a favour owed. The bull has been repaying it.
objectives.reply: Then I shot the bull when it came to the fisherman's door. I am a poor hunter after all. Take the horn back, and set a fish at that door every morning, from me.

quests.outro: There is a fish at the headland door every morning, and no one admits to putting it there.

quests.title: The Wind Has Gone Quiet
quests.offer: Do you feel it? That is not silence. That is attention.
quests.pitch: The wind has gone quiet and I am the only one who thinks it matters. It will speak again if three stones are visited with the right gift: the Wind Stone, the Tree Stone and the Beast Stone. At each, a small thing: a feather, a seed, a claw. Place them and listen.
quests.desc: Wren Wind-Listener asks you to visit three of the All-Maker stones with small gifts.

objectives.text: Take the three gifts from Wren
objectives.topic: I will carry them. Tell me what to say.
objectives.reply: Say nothing. The stones prefer it. Leave the gift at the foot and step back three paces. The wind will tell you if it is pleased.

objectives.text: Leave a feather at the Wind Stone
Leave a seed at the Tree Stone
Leave a claw at the Beast Stone
objectives.journal: At the third stone, the wind lifted. Not a gust. A breath. It stirred the grass, once, and then went on its way over the hills, singing.

objectives.text: Tell Wren the wind has returned
objectives.topic: The wind lifted at the third stone.
objectives.reply: Then it was only waiting to be noticed. It always was. The quiet is back to being a quiet. Thank you. Ketil has a name for it, if you want to hear it. It is Frodi. He may be right.

quests.outro: The wind blew again that night, with the first snow.

quests.title: One More Beast
quests.offer: You walk like a hunter. Do you hunt like one?
quests.pitch: I want a trophy for the rib arch. Not a boar. Not a wolf. Something with a story the bards can sing, a thing with a name. Brynja says there is a snow-boar the size of a hut on the high ridge. Track it. Bring it down. Bring it here, and I will see to it that the hall hangs your name beside the tusk.
quests.desc: Skald Hrolf wants a legendary snow-boar hunted for the hall of Thirsk.

objectives.text: Ask Brynja where the boar was last seen
objectives.topic: The Skald wants a snow-boar. Where?
objectives.reply: The ridge above the Beast Stone. Follow the wallows, count the toppled pines, and when the tracks stop, look up. It likes to watch you come. Do not let it have the high ground.

objectives.text: Track the boar to the ridge above the Beast Stone
objectives.journal: The wallows ran in a ring around a snow-bank. In the middle of it, a toppled pine, and beyond it, a shape so large I took it for a boulder, until it breathed.

objectives.text: Bring down the Snow-Boar
Take the beast's tusk
Bring the tusk to Skald Hrolf
objectives.topic: The beast is down. Here is the tusk.
objectives.reply: A tusk! And such a tusk. Now, the hall must decide how to remember it. I could hang it by the door, and every guest will see it. Or I could break it into drinking-cups, one for every hunter in the hall, so each of us carries a piece. You killed it; you choose.

choices.label: Hang the tusk by the door. Let all see it.
choices.reply: It is a great sight. It will be a great story. And a poor drinking-cup. Done.

choices.label: Break it into cups for every hunter.
choices.reply: Fifty cups of bone. Fifty hunters, every feast, remembering. Perhaps it will do us more good as dust.

quests.outro: The Skald raised the first cup and spilled the first drop for the beast.

quests.title: Odd Dice
quests.offer: Do you gamble? Do you hate being cheated?
quests.pitch: Odd has been cheating at dice for sixty years and nobody has ever caught him. The hall places bets on it, privately. I want him caught, once, in front of everyone, and then forgiven, because he brews the best mead on the island. Be my witness at the next game.
quests.desc: Ingrid Bone-Singer wants to catch Odd the Brewer cheating at dice once, in front of the hall.

objectives.text: Sit down to a game with Odd the Brewer
objectives.topic: A drake a throw?
objectives.reply: A drake a throw. And a free cup for the loser. Do not look at my left hand. It is the same hand. It has been the same hand for sixty years.

objectives.text: Ask Sigrun to look at the dice afterward
objectives.topic: The dice have a weight. Can you tell which?
objectives.reply: Hollow on the six, lead on the one. They were mine; I carved them for his fortieth. I never asked what he did with them. Put them on the anvil and strike: the lead rings.

objectives.text: Tell Ingrid the dice are loaded
objectives.topic: Loaded. And Sigrun will say so in front of the hall.
objectives.reply: Then at the next feast, I shall sing the Ballad of the Honest Dice, and Odd will be astonished at his own talent. He will pay for the meads that night. Nobody will mind.

quests.outro: Odd still cheats. He does it now with a flourish, and the hall applauds.

quests.title: The Boar That Would Not Be Penned
quests.offer: You have the hands for a rope. Do you have the nerve?
quests.pitch: A boar broke the fence at the trophy yard last night and took the oldest rib-beam with it, pinned on a tusk. It is not an escape. It is a theft. The beam is the first rib the hall ever hung. Find it, bring it back, and do not hurt the boar. It is the Skald's, and he is sentimental about pigs.
quests.desc: A boar has fled the trophy yard of Thirsk with the hall's oldest rib-beam on its tusk.

objectives.text: Follow the broken-fence trail toward Vahlok's Tomb
objectives.journal: Trotters in the snow, deep prints, and a long scrape where a beam was dragged. The boar stood at the tomb mouth, the beam still on its tusk, pleased with itself.

objectives.text: Wear the boar down without hurting it
Recover the oldest rib-beam
Return the beam to Sigrun
objectives.topic: The beam. Not a scratch.
objectives.reply: A scratch on the left. It has been there since the founding. Good. The boar was only taking it home. It was its grandfather's, the story goes. Whatever you say.

quests.outro: The boar was re-penned, and then given a better fence, at the Skald's own expense.

quests.title: A Spore for a Spore
quests.offer: Ah. A person with hands. Come in, mind the floor, mind the walls, mind everything.
quests.pitch: My tower grows by a rule: for every spore it gives, it asks one back. I have run out of ones to give. I want three: a glow-gill from the Ashfallow ruin, a whisper-moss from the stone, and an ember-stalk from the black altar. Do not eat them. Do not smell them. If you smell them, I will know.
quests.desc: Magister Ildar of Tel Mithryn needs three rare fungi to feed his tower.

objectives.text: Gather a glow-gill from the Ashfallow ruin
Gather a whisper-moss from the Sun Stone
Gather an ember-stalk from the black altar
Help Duvren stabilise the test chamber
objectives.topic: I have the three. What do you need?
objectives.reply: Hold the lamp. When the chamber breathes, count to four, then drop the glow-gill into the bowl. If the chamber growls, drop the whisper-moss. If it screams, drop the ember-stalk and run.

objectives.text: Quell the test chamber when it wakes
Present the spores to Magister Ildar
objectives.topic: You asked for three. They are in the bowl.
objectives.reply: Good. Now, the choice. I may tutor you in the safe way, which takes a year and teaches little. Or in the reckless way, which takes a week and may kill you. My uncle would choose the second. I am not my uncle. But I would very much like to be.

choices.label: The safe tutor. Take the year.
choices.reply: Dull. Wise. Take this tome and read it twice. You will thank me in eleven months.

choices.label: The reckless tutor. A week, and a prayer.
choices.reply: Ha! I knew you had it. Hold on to something.

quests.outro: The tower hummed, and a new room grew on the second floor, apparently by itself.

quests.title: Rumours for Cake
quests.offer: Cake. Do you have cake? I deal in rumours, and rumours want cake.
quests.pitch: I have three rumours and one cake-sized hole in my stomach. The first: a ship wrecked west of Raven Rock with a Telvanni crest. The second: a Nord on the road asking after the Magister by his old name. The third: I will not say it until the cake. Fetch cake from Raven Rock and I will tell you everything.
quests.desc: Yarda Net-Girl sells rumours for cake. Fetch her some from Raven Rock.

objectives.text: Buy cake from Tindra Hael at Raven Rock
objectives.topic: A cake. For a girl who sells rumours.
objectives.reply: A honey-cake, then, for a rumour. She does not know I have a rumour of my own. I will trade you both: take the cake, and I shall tell you where the wreck is.

objectives.text: Bring the cake to Yarda
objectives.topic: Cake. And a rumour of my own in return.
objectives.reply: The third rumour is that the Magister's nephew keeps a second mushroom in the cellar that eats compliments. Tell him he looks well. Watch what happens. That is all. That is the whole rumour. I am sorry.

quests.outro: The cellar mushroom grew a little, and Ildar looked unwell.

quests.title: Thaw
quests.offer: You look like someone who can walk on ice and not on fools.
quests.pitch: The supply sledge from Raven Rock was due four days ago. The ice is thin and the road is a lie. I need the sledge here by dusk. And I need whoever opened my gate last night to be found before the thaw-raiders try it again. The Legion does not ask nicely. I am asking.
quests.desc: Commander Hale needs the garrison resupplied over thin ice and a gate-opener found.

objectives.text: Collect the supply sledge at Raven Rock's gate
Haul the sledge across the thin ice to the fort
objectives.journal: The ice sang under my boots. Twice it cracked. The sledge went across at a run, and I went after it, and neither of us looked back.

objectives.text: Hold the gate against the thaw-raiders
Ask Signaller Tisa who opened the gate
objectives.topic: Someone opened the gate. Who had the pin?
objectives.reply: Five flashes, sera, from the south lantern, at the third bell. The pin was pulled by someone with a key. The key-holders are four: the commander, the chef, the armourer and me. I did not do it. Check the chef's pot.

objectives.text: Find the gate pin in the chef's stockpot
Present the pin to Commander Hale
objectives.topic: The pin was in the stockpot. The chef did it.
objectives.reply: Orsk. Orsk, who has fed this garrison for eleven years. I have a choice. I can take the blame myself, say I left the pin in a careless hand, and keep him fed and loyal. Or I can place it with him, and be rid of a man who opened the gate for a girl in the snow, by his own account. Which would you do, stranger?

choices.label: Take the blame. The commander owns his gate.
choices.reply: That is not what honour is. It is what loyalty is. Do not tell Orsk I said that.

choices.label: Place it with Orsk. He opened the gate; he answers for it.
choices.reply: Then he answers. The garrison will go hungry for a week. Nobody died. That is the part I will hold on to.

quests.outro: The ice held. The wall held. The stockpot was inspected thoroughly.

quests.title: Five Flashes at Midnight
quests.offer: You are not Legion. You are not afraid of the dark. Good.
quests.pitch: At midnight, five flashes come from the old watch-tower on the ridge, from a lantern the Legion does not own. Five means the gate is open. It is not. It means someone out there is lying to us, in code, and has a very steady hand. I want to know who.
quests.desc: Signaller Tisa sees five flashes from a ridge tower nobody should be in.

objectives.text: Climb the ridge tower at midnight
objectives.journal: A tarnished lantern, a tin of oil, and a girl of fourteen with a bundle of letters. She was signalling her father, who died here, to say her mother was well.

objectives.text: Tell Tisa what the signals were
objectives.topic: A girl in the old tower. She was writing to her father.
objectives.reply: Then I shall flash back, two, then three, then one: all well. The Legion has a code for that. It has never used it.

quests.outro: The old tower lantern is now lit every night. Tisa answers.

quests.title: The Glow-Off
quests.offer: You have eyes. Use them. Which of these is brighter?
quests.pitch: The Magister swears his tower-cap glows brighter than my garden. I swear my garden outshines his tower. Once a year we hold a contest and he cheats with a lamp. Be the judge. And fetch me a proper glow-dust from the Sun Stone first; I will not lose on a technicality.
quests.desc: Pelli Sporeheart and Magister Ildar want a judge for their annual contest of whose lights are brighter.

objectives.text: Gather glow-dust at the Sun Stone for Pelli
objectives.journal: Dust like crushed teal glass, warm as breath, in the cracks of the stone.

objectives.text: Ask Magister Ildar what he is hiding in the cap
objectives.topic: Pelli says you cheat with a lamp.
objectives.reply: A lamp! A lamp, she says. It is a sophisticated luminous apparatus. It is, I admit, shaped like a lamp. Judge fairly. Judge, please, before dusk, when the effect is best.

objectives.text: Judge the Glow-Off
objectives.topic: Both are very bright. I must choose.
objectives.reply: Choose, then. I shall be gracious in defeat. I shall be gracious in defeat for approximately an hour.

choices.label: The garden. It needs no lamp.
choices.reply: Ha! A garden wins. He will sulk for a week. A good week.

choices.label: The tower. He has earned it with sheer nerve.
choices.reply: Nerve! It is true. He shall be unbearable. I shall bake him a cake and put salt in it.

quests.outro: Both lights burned until dawn, and nobody slept.

quests.title: Forty Pairs of Boots
quests.offer: Do you know the sound a hundred boots make leaving? I do now.
quests.pitch: Forty pairs of winter boots, vanished from the armoury in one night, and not a lock forced. I do not believe in thieves who leave no tracks. I believe in thieves who leave tracks leading somewhere else. Look east, toward the old farmhouse where the snow is too clean.
quests.desc: Armourer Decimus Ravo of Fort Frostmoth is missing forty pairs of boots, and a trail of snow that is too clean.

objectives.text: Follow the too-clean trail to Hrodulf's House
objectives.journal: The snow had been brushed smooth with a branch, from the fort gate to the farmhouse step. The thief had been careful, and kind; he had not wanted anyone to follow the tracks and be cold.

objectives.text: Ask Signaller Tisa who lives at Hrodulf's House
objectives.topic: Who is at the old farmhouse?
objectives.reply: An old Nord, a cobbler once, who lost his sons on a patrol. He has nobody to cobble for. I think he took the boots to re-sole them. I think he is lonely.

objectives.text: Tell Decimus about the cobbler
objectives.topic: The boots are at the farmhouse. The cobbler is re-soling them.
objectives.reply: Re-soling. Forty pairs. For a garrison he has never met. I should be furious. I find I am only embarrassed. I shall pay him in barley, and I shall put him on the quartermaster's list, and I shall never mention the chimney.

choices.label: Let him keep a pair for himself.
choices.reply: It is the least we can do. He has earned them, forty times over.

choices.label: Hire him as the fort cobbler, with a stipend.
choices.reply: A cobbler at the fort. Well. It will be warm for him. Good.

quests.outro: The boots were returned with new soles and a note: "For the boys."
